title: How to Trade Breakouts (Failure to Manipulate)
description: Learn failure to manipulate, range breakouts, protected swings, CISD, candle closures, and fractal model entries for continuation trades.

body.text: Introduction
A range can give you two different opportunities. Price can manipulate one side of the range, form a reversal, and trade toward the other side. Or price can take that high or low and fail to reverse.
That second situation is a failure to manipulate.

When price takes a high or low and fails to form a reversal, the expectation changes. Instead of looking for price to reverse back into the range, we can look for continuation and a breakout in the direction price is already moving.
What Is a Failure to Manipulate?
A failure to manipulate happens when price takes out a high or low and fails to form the reversal you would normally expect at that level.
If price takes a high, the normal expectation is that price could manipulate that high, reverse lower, and trade toward the other side of the range.
But if price takes that high and cannot form a bearish change in the state of delivery, there is no reversal to trade.
That failure itself becomes information.
If price is failing to reverse lower, where is it likely to go?
Higher.
The same logic applies when price takes a low and fails to reverse higher. If the bullish reversal never forms, continuation lower becomes the expectation.
Watch the Structure After the Sweep
The sweep itself is not the trade.
After price takes a high or low, watch what happens next.
If price forms an aggressive move in the opposite direction, followed by a change in the state of delivery, that can confirm the manipulation and reversal.
But if price consolidates, retraces, or continues expanding in the same direction without forming that reversal, you may be looking at a failure to manipulate.
This is where patience matters. Wait for the candle closures before deciding what the market is doing.
Let the structure form first.
The Reversal Has to Actually Form
If price takes a high and you are looking for a bearish reversal, you need to see bearish structure develop.
That means looking for price to close back through the series of candles that led into the high and form a bearish change in the state of delivery.
If that never happens, there is no confirmed reversal.
Price can continue making new highs, creating bullish continuations and protected swings along the way.
That is the failure to manipulate.
The same thing happens at a low. If price takes the low but never produces the bullish change in the state of delivery needed to reverse higher, the market may simply continue lower.
Use the Lower Timeframe to Confirm
The lower timeframe can help determine whether the reversal is actually forming.
For example, if price takes a low and you are looking for a bullish manipulation, drop to the lower timeframe and watch for the change in the state of delivery.
If price takes the low, closes back above the candles that took out that low, and forms a protected swing, the reversal can be confirmed.
But if price fails to do that and instead creates a new bearish continuation, that is telling you the level was not manipulated for a reversal.
Use the lower timeframe structure to see whether price is reversing or continuing.
Trade the Continuation
Once the failure to manipulate is confirmed, the trade is no longer about fading the level.
The opportunity becomes the continuation.

Price has taken the high or low, failed to reverse, and formed new continuation structure. That gives you a way to get on side with the breakout rather than trying to force a reversal that never formed.
A continuation can give you a new protected swing to use for the entry and the stop.
The breakout is not the trade just because price crosses a level. The trade comes from price failing to form the reversal that would have taken it back through the range.
Pair It With Higher Timeframe Bias
Failure to manipulate is not a standalone model.
Structure tells you what price is doing, but the higher timeframe tells you why you should be looking for that direction in the first place.
If you are trying to trade a bullish failure to manipulate, you want a reason to be bullish from the higher timeframe. The same applies when looking for a bearish continuation.
This is where the concept fits into the fractal model.
The higher timeframe provides the bias and the lower timeframe provides the structure confirmation.
Without that higher timeframe reason, you are just blindly trading breakouts.
Use Candle Closures
Candle closures are what keep the process mechanical.
If price takes a level, do not assume the reversal has formed. Wait for the candle closure.
If you are looking for a reversal and the candle cannot close through the level you need, the reversal is not confirmed.
If price instead continues and creates a new continuation, that failure to reverse becomes part of the setup.
The same process can be applied across different timeframes because the model is fractal.
Know the Difference
The easiest way to frame the concept is to ask one question after price takes a high or low:
Did the reversal actually form?
If yes, you can look for the manipulation and reversal.
If no, do not force the reversal.
Instead, watch for continuation structure and look for price to expand in the direction it is already moving.
That distinction keeps you from automatically fading every high or low that gets swept.
The Logic Is Fractal
The same process can happen on the daily, hourly, 30 minute, 15 minute, or 1 minute timeframe.
Price reaches a level.
The level gets taken.
You wait for the reversal.
If the reversal forms, you can trade the manipulation.
If the reversal fails to form, you can look for continuation.
The timeframe changes, but the logic stays the same.
Final Thoughts
A failure to manipulate is not simply a breakout.
It is the failure of price to form the reversal you were expecting after taking a high or low.
That failure gives you information. If price cannot reverse, look for the continuation that follows.
Pair the structure with higher timeframe bias, wait for the candle closures, and use the lower timeframe to confirm the new protected swing before getting on side.
The key is to let price show you which scenario is actually forming. If the reversal never develops and price continues instead, that is where the failure to manipulate becomes actionable.
Trade the continuation once the structure confirms it.
